To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic spinal cord hemisection up-regulates ventral spinal serotonin 2A receptors, which is further increased by exposure to chronic, intermittent hypoxia.
chronic C2 spinal cord hemisection (a rat model of cervical spinal cord injury) upregulates 5-HT2a receptors in ventral cervical gray matter.
chronic C2 spinal cord injury upregulated 5-HT2a receptors in the spinal segments that contain the phrenic motor neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and plasticity of the crossed phrenic pathway, and its role in the recovery of breathing after spinal cord injury (SCI).
the role of serotonin in the recovery of function following spinal cord injury (SCI).
the role of 5-HT2 receptors in the development of cross-spinal phrenic pathways following C2HS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 5-HT2AR is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of respiratory dysfunction following SCI.
CIH exposure enhances 5-HT2AR expression in ventral spinal segments containing phremic motoneurons ipsilateral and contralatral to C2HS.
the spinal 5-HT system, including its receptors, is upregulated following cervical spinal injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic C2 spinal cord injury and CIH increase 5-HT2AR expression on or near the phrenic nucleus and that this may contribute to the spontaneous increase in efficacy of crossed spinal pathways to the phrenic motor pool.
CIH exposure enhances 5-HT2AR-mediated synaptic plasticity in spinal segments that are injured or spared following spinal hemisection.
chronic C2 spinal cord hemisection (2 weeks) increases ventral spinal 2A receptors in a region of spinal gray matter containing phrenic motor neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-HT2 receptor expression is increased in ventral spinal cord following C2 spinal injury, and that CIH exposure further augments 5-HT2 expression in the contralateral spinal cord.
5-HT2ARs play a key role in the plasticity associated with spinal cord injury.
